facts.name: Rocky Face Mountain (summit / peak)
facts.what: The named summit of Rocky Face Mountain, a dome-shaped granite mass (granitic dome / bornhardt formed by exfoliation) at the southern edge of the Brushy Mountains. High point of the park, roughly 600 ft above surrounding terrain. The Hollow Rock Trail loops around the peak.
facts.elevation: ~1,795 ft (TopoZone/waypoint); local sources ~1,800 ft max; GNIS elevation field differs (~1,217 ft, likely datum/base discrepancy)
facts.access: Reached via park trail system (Grindstone Trail connects to Hollow Rock Trail at the top); ~5-6 miles of trails. Within the county park, all within ~3 miles of NC-16 / Vashti Rd.

facts.name: The Quarry (former Rocky Face quarry) / the cliff face
facts.what: Man-made crag created by granite-gneiss quarrying (operated 1922 to early 1940s, worked partly by prison labor; gravel/rock loaded into railroad cars). The sheer vertical cliff face rises 80-100 ft and is the dominant rock feature and main climbing destination (58+ established routes). Now hosts the park picnic area, restrooms, and climbing/rappelling facilities.
facts.coords: approx 35.9723,-81.1087 (Rocky Face Quarry Prospect, Hiddenite, mindat)
facts.access: Accessible from the parking lot / quarry area; a 1/3-mile paved ADA walking track runs through the former quarry. Climbing/rappelling require a daily permit from the Park Office; climbers must be off the wall 30 min before closing.

facts.name: Quarry Overlook (rock staircase overlook)
facts.what: Overlook reached by climbing ~100 ft via a rock staircase on the west side of the old quarry; the Buzzard Loop trail begins and ends at this rock staircase. View down over the quarry cliffs.
facts.elevation: ~100 ft above quarry floor / parking area
facts.access: Trail begins at the rock staircase in/near the parking lot; easy-to-moderate. Within the park.

facts.name: Hollow Rock (summit ridge feature and overlooks)
facts.what: Named rock feature/area along the summit ridge. The Hollow Rock Trail runs across the full length of the ridge and loops around Rocky Face's peak, crossing large expanses of exposed granite with views in all directions. Visible from its overlooks: Pores Knob (2,680 ft, tallest in the Brushies, to the north), Fletcher, Snaggy, Mitchell, Moore mountains in Wilkes; to the west Grandfather, Table Rock, Hawksbill, and distant Black Mountain peaks on clear days.
facts.access: Hollow Rock Trail (red), ~2.5-mile round trip / ~3.1-mile loop, moderate-to-strenuous; connects to Grindstone Trail. Within the park.

facts.name: Vertical Mile Challenge Trail (open granite face)
facts.what: Trail featuring a ~350-ft climb up an open exposed granite face (compared to the granite-face climb at Stone Mountain State Park but without assisting stairs). A standout bare-rock walking feature.
facts.coords: unknown (open granite face of the mountain)
facts.elevation: ~350 ft of vertical gain over open granite
facts.access: Reached via Quarry Trail then Grindstone Trail then Vertical Mile Trail. Within the park.

facts.name: Rocky Face - Left Face (climbing area; Sections 1-2)
facts.what: Named climbing area on the left side of the cliff/mountain. Section 1 routes: Short Stack (5.6), Far Left Corner (5.6), Too Short (5.7), Leaky Roof (5.6), Bob Left (5.6), Bob Right (5.8), Bob's Gone Batty (5.8), Ben's Done Been (5.8+), Chaos in Carolina (5.9), One Step (5.9), Klingon (5.9), Hang Time (5.6), Pork Chop (5.6), Chopped Pork (5.7).
facts.access: Accessed from the trail around the left side of the mountain; follow trail to the end of the cables and turn right. Daily climbing permit required.

facts.name: Rocky Face - Bottom Ledge (climbing area; Sections 3-4)
facts.what: Named climbing area at the bottom of the quarry. Section 3 includes Confederate Daisies (5.4), Left at the Y (5.2), Twin Turbo (5.4), Jug Land (5.5), Lady Bug Corner (5.5). Section 4 includes Gateway (5.4), Gateway Direct (5.6), Dirty Chimney (5.5), Left of Time (5.7), Flight Time (5.7+), Black Hole (5.10+), Mr. Aidmans Free (5.11a), Double Roof Ballet (5.11b), Hardman (5.11b), Quickdraw (5.11c), Crimps and Slopers (5.10b/c), Blast in Black (5.9+), Quarryisms (5.10c/d), Ramped Up (TR, not currently open).
facts.access: Accessed from the bottom of the quarry. Daily climbing permit required.

facts.name: Rocky Face - Section 5 (climbing area)
facts.what: Additional named climbing section on the cliff, containing routes including Lightning Crack and Snake Charmer.
facts.access: On the main cliff; daily climbing permit from the Park Office required.

facts.name: Two wildlife observation decks (wetlands)
facts.what: Two wildlife observation decks in the park's wetlands/wetland-restoration area, accessed via boardwalks. Lower-elevation named standing points (not on the cliff).
facts.coords: unknown (lower wetland area of the park)
facts.access: Boardwalks through the wetland area, near the developed/lower portion of the park.

facts.name: Outdoor amphitheater
facts.what: Outdoor amphitheater within the park's developed core; a defined named structure a person can stand at, near the community/multipurpose building.
facts.access: Developed park core near the multipurpose building and playground.

facts.name: Adventure playground (zip cord / large slide)
facts.what: Children's 'adventure' playground with a zip cord and a large slide in the developed park area; a clearly named, locatable spot.
facts.access: Developed park core, near picnic shelters and parking.

facts.name: Prison Camp Trail (historic prison-camp site)
facts.what: Moderate trail winding through a historically significant area that once served as a prison camp in the mid-20th century (tied to the quarry's prison-labor history). A named, place-specific historical spot on the mountain.
facts.access: Prison Camp Trail (~1 mile), part of the interconnected trail network. Within the park.

facts.name: Rocky Face Mountain Recreational Area (park envelope)
facts.what: ~318-acre Alexander County park (largest publicly owned tract in the Brushy Mountains), opened 2012, containing the summit, cliff/quarry, ~5-6 miles of trails, named climbing sections, wetlands, amphitheater, playground, picnic shelters, primitive campsite, and park office.
facts.coords: park address 3451 Rocky Face Church Road, Hiddenite, NC 28636
facts.elevation: park spans up to ~1,795 ft summit
facts.access: Public county park at 3451 Rocky Face Church Rd, Hiddenite. From Wilkesboro: south on NC-16 through Moravian Falls; ~3 miles past the county line turn left onto Vashti Road. Hours ~8am-8pm; phone 828-632-1093.
